candidates.summary: findChrome's os.Stat fallback sits at the wrong depth: LookPath already tries a slashed path directly, so the only candidate Stat adds is one that exists and cannot be executed, and returning it converts a clean skip into an exec failure per screenshot
candidates.failure_scenario: exec.LookPath tries a file containing a slash directly, so /Applications/Google Chrome.app/... resolves through LookPath whenever it is runnable. The Stat branch therefore fires only when the path exists and LookPath rejected it, meaning no exec permission; findChrome then returns it, bin != "", and every chromeShot exec fails with permission denied, printing '! screenshot <url>: ...' per page instead of the one '! no Chrome/Chromium found' line the design intends. For a bare name like "chromium" it is worse: Stat resolves it against the working directory, and exec.Command with no separator looks it up on PATH again, so the value returned cannot be run at all.
candidates.verify_by: go doc os/exec.LookPath for the slash rule, then in a scratch dir: touch chromium && chmod -x chromium, and call findChrome("") with CHROME unset from the package's working directory; observe a non-empty return whose exec fails
candidates.evidence: go doc os/exec.LookPath: "If file contains a slash, it is tried directly and the PATH is not consulted." Not run as a program: a Nit is read, not run, per the finder rules.
